**Issue #2022 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2022: Patch: the rank reads fetch only the players they show and the Mythic rows, not the whole season's ladder
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The server does three things often: open a match screen, open your rank, and file the statistics of every finished game. Each time, it reads the ranked standing of every player in the current season, joins each to their profile and rating, and then keeps one or two rows plus the top-tier players.

As the ladder fills over a season, that work grows with it, on some of the most frequent reads the server makes. Once this is built, those reads fetch only the players they need and the top-tier rows a leaderboard position comes from. Nothing on screen changes; the server does far less work per match as the season grows.

## Why
- `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:5784-5797` `ranked_standings` filters only `where r.season_id = $1::text`. It joins `profiles` and `bot_ratings`, then turns every row into a `serde_json::Value` and back (`:5800-5810`).
- Three frequent callers each use one or two rows of it, plus the Jlorious order:
  - `api/ranked.rs:726` `own_rank` (GET /api/ranked);
  - `api/ranked.rs:922` `match_ranks` (GET /api/matches/:id/ranks, which the match screens read);
  - `api/ranked.rs:950` `ladder_tiers`, called for the play telemetry of every match (`actor/match_actor.rs:702`, then `actor/telemetry.rs:362`).
- What they actually need:
  - `rank_in` (`api/ranked.rs:660`) finds one profile's row;
  - `jlorious_order` (`ranked/ladder.rs:386-406`) keeps only Mythic-tier, non-bot rows, sorted by rating then id, `take(JLORIOUS_SIZE)`.
- `migrations/0022_ranked_ladder.sql` gives `season_ranks` only its primary key `(season_id, profile_id)` and a profile index, so nothing serves a read by tier.
- #1996 made the queue's waiting-room readout read through indexes instead of every game ever played. This is the same kind of fix for the rank reads.

## Proposal
- Add a store method returning a season's rows for the given profile ids, plus every row at or above the Mythic floor, with the same rating join and `bot` flag (R640000).
  - The floor is `tier_bottom(MYTHIC)` from `ranked/ladder.rs`, passed as a bind, never restated in SQL.
  - `jlorious_order` and `rank_in` stay in Rust unchanged, so sorting, ties and NaN ratings behave exactly as today.
- Use it in `own_rank`, `match_ranks` and `ladder_tiers`. The rated-game plan (`api/ranked.rs:392`, which needs every rating for percentiles) and the leaderboard (R612 lists everyone) stay on `ranked_standings`.
- Add a migration with an index on `season_ranks (season_id, ladder)`, so the Mythic read is an index range rather than a scan of the season.
- The in-memory fake store implements the same filter.

## Where it lands
- `crates/server/src/db/store.rs`, `pg.rs`, `fake.rs`
- `crates/server/src/api/ranked.rs`
- a new migration under `crates/server/migrations/`
- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` and the ranked API tests
- SPEC §9.12 (ranked): unchanged

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `tests/store/contract.rs` case, run on both stores. Its season holds ladder bots, rating ties, unplaced players, players below Mythic, and more Mythic rows than `JLORIOUS_SIZE`. With it:
  - `jlorious_order` over the new read equals `jlorious_order` over the full read;
  - `rank_in` is the same for every profile asked for.
- [ ] GET /api/ranked and GET /api/matches/:id/ranks return identical bodies before and after, in the existing API tests.
- [ ] `own_rank`, `match_ranks` and `ladder_tiers` no longer call `ranked_standings`.
- [ ] `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh` and `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` pass with the migration.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server`, clippy and fmt pass.

## Size and risks
Medium: about 6 files in one crate plus a migration (the migration is what CLAUDE.md rule 11 calls hard).

Risks:
- The Mythic floor must come from the ladder code, or the two can drift.
- A ladder bot's row must keep reading the bot's own rating.
- The migration turns on the db suites in CI.
- The gain grows with the season's size and is small while the ladder is small.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

<!-- jackioh-bot -->

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40423814151)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Replace the season-wide `ranked_standings` read in the three hot rank reads with a subset read that fetches only the rows it needs: the requested profiles' rows plus every row at or above the Mythic floor (the pool Jlorious is drawn from). `own_rank` (GET /api/ranked), `match_ranks` (GET /api/matches/:id/ranks) and `ladder_tiers` (per-match play telemetry) return byte-identical bodies while scanning a bounded slice of the season instead of all of it. The rated-game planner, the leaderboard and the bot-pool grind planner stay on the full read. A composite index on `season_ranks (season_id, ladder)` serves the Mythic range. SPEC §9.12 is unchanged and no ruling is added: nothing observable changes.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/server/src/db/store.rs` | change | New `Tx` method `ranked_standings_subset`, next to `ranked_standings` (~line 2285), via `dispatch!` |
| `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs` | change | New `ranked_standings_subset` beside `ranked_standings` (~line 5868): same select/join/rating mapping, narrower `where` |
| `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs` | change | New `ranked_standings_subset` beside `ranked_standings` (~line 3646) with the same filter |
| `crates/server/src/api/ranked.rs` | change | Private `mythic_floor()` helper; `own_rank`, `match_ranks`, `ladder_tiers` switch to the subset read |
| `crates/server/migrations/0064_ranked_subset_index.sql` | new | `season_ranks_season_ladder_idx` on `(season_id, ladder)` |
| `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs` | change | Register `0064_ranked_subset_index.sql` in `MIGRATIONS` after the `0063` entry |
| `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` | change | New case in `mod ranked` plus one line in its `both_stores!` list |
| `crates/server/tests/api/ranked.rs` | change | New test asserting the three reads never call `ranked.standings` |
| `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` | change | One `PINNED` line with the new migration's checksum |

Do not touch: `crates/server/src/bots/pool.rs` (stays on the full read), `plan_ranked_game` and `leaderboard` in `api/ranked.rs`, `crates/server/src/ranked/ladder.rs`, anything under `spec/`, `crates/engine/`, `crates/cards/`, `crates/ai/`, `apps/web/`. Governing spec: SPEC §9.12 with R605–R612, R640000, R1436; no new ruling.

## Steps

1. In `crates/server/src/db/store.rs`, after `ranked_standings` (~line 2288), add:
   ```rust
   /// The rows three hot reads need (issue #2022): the asked profiles' rows, plus every row
   /// at or above `mythic_floor`, each with the player's current rating, in profile-id order.
   /// `jlorious_order` and `rank_in` over this answer equal the full read's, so callers keep them.
   pub async fn ranked_standings_subset(&mut self, season_id: &str, profile_ids: &[String], mythic_floor: i32) -> StoreResult<Vec<SeasonStanding>> {
       dispatch!(self, ranked_standings_subset(season_id, profile_ids, mythic_floor))
   }
   ```
2. In `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, after `ranked_standings`, add `pub async fn ranked_standings_subset(t: &mut PgTx<'_>, season_id: &str, profile_ids: &[String], mythic_floor: i32)`. Copy `ranked_standings`' select list, joins (`profiles`, `left join bot_ratings … p.kind = 'bot'` for R640000) and row-mapping closure verbatim; change only the filter to `where r.season_id = $1::text and (r.profile_id = any($2::uuid[]) or r.ladder >= $3)`, keeping `order by r.profile_id`. Bind `.bind(season_id).bind(profile_ids.to_vec()).bind(mythic_floor)`, copying the `any($1::uuid[])` + `.bind(vec)` pattern from `profiles_get_many` (~line 1960). No early return for an empty id list: the Mythic arm must still answer.
3. In `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, after `ranked_standings`, add `pub fn ranked_standings_subset(f: &mut FakeTx<'_>, season_id: &str, profile_ids: &[String], mythic_floor: i32)` with `call(f, "ranked.standingsSubset")?;`, the same season filter, row mapping and bot-rating logic, plus `profile_ids.contains(&row.profile_id) || row.ladder.is_some_and(|ladder| ladder >= mythic_floor)`, sorted with `by_profile_id` exactly as the full read.
4. In `crates/server/src/api/ranked.rs`: add `tier_bottom` to the existing `ladder::{…}` import (`GrapeTier` is already imported) and add a private helper `fn mythic_floor() -> i32 { tier_bottom(GrapeTier::Mythic as i32) }` with a comment that the discriminant-equals-index contract is stated on `GrapeTier` in `ladder.rs`, so the floor cannot drift from the Jlorious pool. Then switch three calls, passing the floor as a value: `own_rank` (~line 726) uses `&[profile_id.to_string()]`; `match_ranks` (~line 921) uses `&[row.players.0.clone(), row.players.1.clone()]` after the match row is read; `ladder_tiers` (~line 949) uses `&[players.0.clone(), players.1.clone()]`. Leave `jlorious_order`, `rank_in`, `standings_of`, `plan_ranked_game` and `leaderboard` untouched.
5. Create `crates/server/migrations/0064_ranked_subset_index.sql` in the style of `0062_queue_readout_indexes.sql` (header comment naming issue #2022, apply order, re-runnable): `create index if not exists season_ranks_season_ladder_idx on public.season_ranks (season_id, ladder);`. Plain composite, not partial: the floor lives in Rust and must never be restated in SQL, and `NULL` ladders never satisfy `>=`, so unplaced rows stay out of the range scan either way.
6. Register the file in `MIGRATIONS` in `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs` after the `0063` tuple, and add its `PINNED` line in `tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` after `0063_game_totals.sql`. Get the checksum by running the pinned test once and copying the computed hash from its failure output; re-run to green.
7. In `tests/store/contract.rs`, `mod ranked`, add case `subset_read_keeps_asked_rows_and_every_mythic_row_and_matches_the_full_read` and list it in that module's `both_stores!`. Seed season `v0.1` with: 105 placed Mythic persons (more than `JLORIOUS_SIZE` 100; two sharing the top rating to cover ties), one Mythic ladder bot (bot profile via `new_bot` + `bots_create` + its own `bot_ratings` row + season row, per the R640000 test's pattern), three below-Mythic persons, one below-Mythic bot, two unplaced persons and one unplaced bot. Ask for four ids (below-Mythic person, unplaced person, unplaced bot, one Mythic person) plus one unknown id (must not error). Assert: every asked id's `SeasonStanding` equals the full read's; every full row with `ladder >= tier_bottom(GrapeTier::Mythic as i32)` is present and equal; no other rows are present; and `jlorious_order` over the two answers (mapped to `Standing` in the test, filtering `!bot` as `standings_of` does) is equal. Those are exactly `rank_in`'s two inputs (own row, Jlorious list), so `rank_in` agrees for every asked profile. Import `Standing`, `GrapeTier`, `tier_bottom`, `jlorious_order` for the test.
8. In `tests/api/ranked.rs`, add a test that sets `fake_lock(&app).await.on_call` to fail any call named `"ranked.standings"` (pattern at `tests/api/replays.rs:744`, reset to `None` after), then calls `own_rank`, the match-ranks HTTP path and `ladder_tiers` on seeded data and asserts success. Do not modify the existing R612/R1436 body assertions: they are the identical-bodies proof.
9. Run: `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store store::contract::ranked`, `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::ranked`, `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store migrations_pinned`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`, `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`.

## Tests

- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, new case `subset_read_keeps_asked_rows_and_every_mythic_row_and_matches_the_full_read` (runs on both stores via `both_stores!`): proves subset/full equivalence of rows and Jlorious with bots, ties, unplaced players, sub-Mythic players and 105 Mythic rows. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store store::contract::ranked`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/ranked.rs`, new test (name it `subset_reads_never_call_the_full_standings_read`): `on_call` hook fails `ranked.standings`; `own_rank`, match ranks and `ladder_tiers` still succeed. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::ranked`.
- Unchanged existing tests `r612_r1436_get_api_ranked_…`, `r612_r1436_get_api_leaderboard_…`, `r612_r1436_get_api_matches_id_ranks_…` prove identical response bodies.
- `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` proves the new migration is registered with the right checksum. `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh` and `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` prove the migration applies and both stores agree.

## Done when

- [ ] Subset read exists on both stores with identical results on the contract case above.
- [ ] `jlorious_order` over the subset equals the full read's with 105 Mythic rows, ties and bots; `rank_in` inputs agree for every asked profile.
- [ ] GET /api/ranked and GET /api/matches/:id/ranks bodies unchanged in the existing API tests.
- [ ] `own_rank`, `match_ranks`, `ladder_tiers` no longer call `ranked_standings` (hook test); planner, leaderboard and bot pool still do.
- [ ] Migration `0064` registered, checksummed and applied in both db suites.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store`, `--test server api::ranked`, clippy and fmt pass; `sql/run.sh` and `db/run.sh` pass.

## Risks

- Floor drift between SQL and Rust: avoided by passing the floor as a bind computed from `tier_bottom(GrapeTier::Mythic as i32)`; the index names no tier and no number.
- Bot rows: the subset query copies the full read's `coalesce(bot_ratings, profiles)` join and `bot` flag, so a ladder bot's row keeps its own rating; Jlorious still filters bots in Rust, unchanged.
- Pool planner (`bots/pool.rs`) needs every person's rating for grind targets, so it deliberately stays on the full read; changing it would corrupt grind planning.
- The gain is proportional to season size and small while the ladder is small; the index adds one write-time cost per rank upsert.
- `ranked_standings_subset` as a name is a planner choice; the alternative `ranked_subset` was rejected as less discoverable beside `ranked_standings`.

## Open questions

None. No person is needed: no spec change, no ruling, no secret, no dashboard setting, and every file is inside `crates/server/`, which the bot may change.
````
